summary: Misaligned embedding stride causing intermittent rerank queueing and 503s for batch rerank requests
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-11 22:00 UTC AtlasSearch has reported intermittent 503s and large tail latency on the reranking endpoint when they submit batched rerank requests that include freshly ingested embeddings. Impact: Customer-facing search degraded (some queries returned 503 or partial results) and rerank latency spiked from median ~120ms to tail >2s for ~5% of requests. This affects a subset of batched workloads only (batch size >= 32).

Environment: Dedicated cluster rwd-dedicated-us-east-3 serving AtlasSearch tenant. Ingestion path uses the customer's custom SDK (v0.9.3) to upload embeddings; rerank traffic routes through the same dedicated pool.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Ingest 50K vectors using SDK v0.9.3 with batch_size=64 and embedding_stride=2 (customer configuration). 2) Immediately issue concurrent rerank batched requests (batch sizes 32-128) that reference the freshly ingested IDs. 3) Observe rerank endpoint response codes and latency distribution.

Observed behavior: 1) A subset (~3-7%) of rerank requests return 503 with logs indicating internal queue overflow and worker-level checksum mismatch warnings. 2) When 503s do not occur, tail latency increases dramatically and CPU on a small number of replicas spikes. 3) Embedding dimensionality appears correct in API-level responses, but internal vector buffer offsets do not line up with metadata IDs in several traces.

Expected behavior: Rerank should return deterministic results with stable latencies; newly ingested vectors should be immediately queryable without causing queueing or worker checksum warnings.
investigation_notes:
03-12 02:15 UTC - Initial triage by Support: confirmed pattern correlates with customer use of embedding_stride > 1 during ingest and immediate rerank requests. No global outage.
03-12 03:40 UTC - Gathered logs from the serving-runtime replicas pinned to the customer's tenant: repeated WARN entries: "vector_buffer_offset mismatch id=<id> expected_stride=1 got_stride=2" and occasional panic-protected errors leading to 503s.
03-12 05:00 UTC - Replayed ingest on staging with same SDK and embedding_stride=2; observed replicated behavior: extra zero-padding between vectors at write time, but read path assumes compact stride.
03-12 08:30 UTC - Hypothesis: Ingest pipeline honors a deprecated 'embedding_stride' metadata and writes vectors with padding; rerank read path in serving-runtime currently assumes stride=1 (compact), causing read offsets to skip/pick up padding data as part of subsequent vectors, producing checksum warnings and extra CPU while reconstructing vectors. This manifests only under high-occupancy batch loads and when ingestion-to-query latency is low.
03-12 11:20 UTC - Checked scheduler metrics: affected workers show increased queue depth and retry loops in the rerank subroutine when checksum mismatch occurs.
03-13 09:10 UTC - Correlated with SDK v0.9.3 change: a packaging optimization added optional stride/padding to enable memory-aligned writes for some customers. SDK change landed without a corresponding serving-runtime feature flag.
actions_taken:
03-12 12:00 UTC - Eng: Scoped patch to serving-runtime that reads embedding metadata and respects stride during vector reconstruction (hotfix branch).
03-13 02:00 UTC - Deployed temporary mitigation: rate-limit immediate rerank traffic for AtlasSearch tenant (soft limit) to reduce retries and tail latency while fixes are validated; notified customer.
03-13 18:45 UTC - Support requested AtlasSearch to re-ingest a small test namespace with embedding_stride=1; test rerank traffic passed without 503s.
03-14 04:00 UTC - Hotfix PR opened (see related_github_prs).
comments: Maya Patel (2026-03-12 02:30 UTC): Customer reported spikes after last ingest. Collected request IDs and initial traces: rreq-3301, rreq-3302, trace links attached.

Sergio Alvarez (2026-03-12 04:05 UTC): Confirmed WARN lines in replica logs. Pinning to dedicated pool rwd-dedicated-us-east-3-7. Hypothesis: ingest stride/padding mismatch. Eng pinged in #support and #infra.
Elena Kaur (SRE) (2026-03-12 06:10 UTC): Replayed ingest on staging with customer's SDK; saw zero bytes between vectors when embedding_stride=2. Filing an engineer task.
Jason Liu (SDK) (2026-03-13 09:20 UTC): Acknowledged the SDK change in v0.9.3 that introduced optional stride. Working on a client-side guard and a note in the changelog.
Sergio Alvarez (2026-03-13 20:30 UTC): Deployed temporary soft-rate-limit for AtlasSearch to reduce customer impact. Monitoring shows 503s dropped from 6% to ~0.8%.
AtlasSearch (Customer) (2026-03-14 01:15 UTC): We're running the re-ingest test; will confirm by 08:00 local. Thanks for the mitigation.
next_steps: 1) Merge and roll out serving-runtime hotfix that respects embedding stride metadata in the read path (target: 2026-03-15). 2) Add a compatibility check in the ingest API to warn on non-default stride or reject when tenant runtime version does not support stride>1. 3) Publish SDK advisory and release v0.9.4 that disables stride by default and warns users. 4) Ask AtlasSearch to re-ingest production namespace or run a coordinated migration window if they need stride for performance. 5) Postmortem and documentation update to prevent recurrence.
resolution: Workaround in place: temporary soft-rate-limit and customer re-ingest test. Hotfix merged to branch and awaiting staged rollout. Final resolution pending rollout and customer re-ingest.
